data.budget: no paid model calls; web research plus read-only host probes
data.claim: ddflow should own the investigation RECORD (hypothesis, pre-committed prediction and falsifier, probe, verdict validated/refuted/inconclusive, repro bundle, budget cap) and reach tools only through thin optional subprocess adapters; the published evidence says structure and function-level state beat raw debugger access: bare pdb gained 0.8 points at +$0.60 per task while a function-level interface gained 8.8 points at +$0.26 (arXiv 2604.24212), naive reproduction tests did not help patching while multi-faceted runtime-grounded ones did (arXiv 2607.00990), and LLM refinement of decompiled code raised build rate 75 to 90 percent while behavioural match fell 74 to 62 percent (arXiv 2609.05370), so parity needs differential oracles, not build or shipped-test passes.
data.falsifier: On a seeded set of hard bugs in own code, runs using the investigation record plus function-level trace adapter show no better fix rate, and no lower token cost, than the same agent with shell access alone; or an adapter proves unable to keep the sandbox class limits on this host.
data.mechanism: Adapters per r-adapters: sandbox (docker first, gVisor/Firecracker later), debug (DAP via debugpy or mcp-debugger, summarised and capped), reduce (predicate contract shared with git bisect exit codes 0/1-127/125), fuzz/property (Hypothesis, Atheris), trace (py-spy, faulthandler), bench (hyperfine, pyperf), re-readonly (Ghidra headless, rizin). Conflicts to settle: D-reimpl-answers item 4 says read-only adapters but DAP evaluate and Ghidra script tools run code, so those must be withheld or sandbox-only; rr in Docker needs SYS_PTRACE plus a loosened seccomp profile, which weakens r-re-sandbox, so rr is own-code only. Run GPL/AGPL tools as separate processes, never import or vendor them (licence effect inferred, not legal advice).
data.probe: Read-only host probe: command -v for each tool; /proc/sys/kernel/{perf_event_paranoid,yama/ptrace_scope,apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns}; readlink /proc/self/ns/user and Seccomp in /proc/self/status to exclude nesting; bwrap --unshare-all and --unshare-net; docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --memory 256m --pids-limit 64 on local image ddflow:pytest; perf stat; bpftrace; gdb -p on a non-child; gdb --args; py-spy record -- cmd
data.probe_output: PRESENT gdb 15.1, strace, perf, bpftrace, bwrap 0.9.0, docker 29.9.2 (runc, cgroup v2), rootless podman 4.9.3, uv, py-spy 0.4.2, gcc. ABSENT rr valgrind lldb runsc firecracker nix ghidra r2 rizin frida afl-fuzz cvise creduce hyperfine clang. Ubuntu 24.04. perf_event_paranoid=4 and perf stat refused; ptrace_scope=1 and gdb attach to a non-child refused, gdb --args and py-spy launch worked; bpftrace: root only; /dev/kvm exists, not accessible to this user; ulimit -c 0 and core_pattern=apport; apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 and bwrap failed (uid map Permission denied; RTM_NEWADDR not permitted) in the initial user namespace with Seccomp 0, so not a nesting artefact; docker no-network, read-only, cap-drop run succeeded.
data.question: What external practice and tooling (2026) should ddflow adopt to debug applications, libraries, snippets and tests, investigate hard bugs, do lawful reverse engineering and validate hypotheses, and what should go through adapters versus be left alone?
